findings.title: After a boss, choosing the Hitcher's service puts nobody at the roadside

D-037: 'a TAP on one makes the boss stop that stop' and 'Hitcher. Two minutes and nothing to buy until the passengers of M8.'
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/m8rev-tests-views/probes/sim_probes.gd, section boss_stop_hitcher: Telling seed 31 driven to the stop after Act 1's boss, the free pick taken and placed with the hand, then a TAP on the service 'hitcher'. It printed: 'his free pick (fifth_gear) is his; the services held out: fuel_station, fitter, tea_stall, roadside_find, hitcher' then 'he taps the Hitcher: the stop's service is now 'passenger'; offers on the tray 0; at the roadside: ''; the door can be unlocked: false' then 'a TAP on the passenger door: boarded 0, passenger '''.
findings.failure: Three times a night the player may spend his one free service on a Hitcher. The tray empties, nobody stands at the roadside, the door stays locked and the choice is gone: he gave up tea or a repair for nothing.
findings.fix: When the boss stop takes on a stop record whose 'hitcher' is set, draw who stands there: StopSim keeps the id of the stop chosen, and DriveSim._complete_ritual, after `stop.buy`, sets `stop.hitcher = RunGenerator.hitcher(data, run.seed, run.act, run.legs_done, <that id>, passengers.id)` and calls `_sync_anchors()`. Append a case to T-STOP-01 or T-PASS-HAJJIYA: at a boss stop he chooses 'hitcher', somebody stands there, the door unlocks, they board, the Clock stands.

findings.title: The Apprentice's Hand does nothing in play: 'its current angle' is always 0, and the test gets its 30 degrees by setting the wheel after the reach
findings.where: src/core/passenger_sim.gd:280-282 (the hold begins when the TAP lands); src/core/drive_sim.gd:432; tests/test_passengers.gd:1047-1071 (line 1048 `_reach(SHOULDER)`, then line 1049 `_sim.wheel.reset(30.0)`)
findings.gdd: GDD 8.2: 'On a tap he holds the wheel at its current angle for 3 s.' GDD 4.3: 'On release the wheel returns to centre at 200 degrees per second'. GDD 16.2: passenger_shoulder 0.53 s. D-043 on the same words for the Wheel ring: 'Read literally ... the hook would be useless: the hand must leave the wheel to tap it, and a wheel let go is back at centre before any TAP can land'. D-051 says he locks the wheel 'as the hook does'; the hook is hung first and takes the wheel as the hand leaves it.
findings.evidence: sim_probes.gd in the same probes folder, section apprentice_angles, through the input (grip, steer, let go, reach his shoulder, TAP): steered to 29.9, 59.9, 89.8 and 119.8 degrees, the wheel is at 0.0 degrees when the hand arrives (0.52 to 0.62 s after letting go) and at 0.0 when he holds it; from full lock, 134.8 degrees, it is at 6.4 on arrival and 0.0 when held (0.683 s). Section apprentice_hand_worth, steered to 60 degrees, let go, hand to his shoulder: 'not asked: wheel_held=0; ... 3.5 s after letting go the car is 1.4417 m from where it was let go' and 'asked: wheel_held=2; ... 1.4417 m'. The same road with and without his Hand.
findings.failure: A player asks the boy to hold the wheel in a bend and nothing changes: the wheel is already back at the centre, and the car drifts exactly as with nobody holding it. One of his two Hands is empty. T-PASS-APPRENTICE says otherwise because it puts the wheel at 30 degrees while the hand is already on his shoulder, which no input can do.
findings.fix: Hold the angle the wheel had when his hand left it: DriveSim remembers `wheel.angle` at `hand.let_go`, and when ask() gives HOLD_ANGLE within about a second and before he has gripped again it calls `wheel.hold_at(that angle)`. Record the ruling in D-051 (the owner should see it). Append a check that steers to 60 degrees with `_grip` and `_steer`, lets go, taps his shoulder with no `wheel.reset`, and expects the angle he let go at to be held and the car's path to differ from hands off.

findings.title: Nine checks in T-PASS that cannot fail
findings.gdd: docs/CLAUDE.md, test rules: 'A test must establish the passes_when text of its entry in tests/tests.json, with failure cases'. GDD 1.4 rule 4.
findings.evidence: (a) Line 588, 'and no ritual time': `float(_sim.tick - asked_at) * DT < 0.1` measures the helper's own wait. sim_probes_2.gd section ask_ticks prints '_sim.tick - asked_at = 4 ticks (0.0333 s): the helper's own SETTLE (4)' for all five. (b) Lines 916-917, after the Student has left: N11 (`_hold_statuses()` removed from _empty_seat) and N12 (`_items.answered_for_him = false` removed) are ALIVE, because the stop rebuilds the whole simulation. (c) Line 162, '(never the one he carries)': N31 (`passengers.id` becomes `""` in _open_stop) is ALIVE: the seed is chosen so that the draw is `who`, and the one in the seat is somebody else by construction. (d) Lines 751 and 1116, 'he pays nothing', compare cash across leaving a stop in two identical runs: M1 (one who rides to Basra pays 50 on getting in) and M2 (pays 50 at Basra) are ALIVE. (e) Line 819 reads `answered` of the last call_resolved, which is false when there was no call: M3 (the phone never rings unless she is there) is ALIVE. (f) Line 435 counts passenger_left with nobody in the seat. (g) Line 199 asks one seed at a stop whose record names no hitcher. Logs: logs/new_mutants.log and logs/new_mutants_2.log in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/m8rev-tests-views/.
findings.failure: The report counts 'no ritual time', 'he pays nothing', 'food once' and 'never the one he carries' as established; a change that broke any of them would pass.
findings.fix: Append: (a) the cigarette burns in the very tick `ritual_completed` appears, beside a control lit with the lighter that burns one hold_s later; (c) a seed whose plain draw is the one riding, where the roadside must show another of the five; (d) the night's cash at the last street against the same night without him, as the Conscript's check does; (e) `check_eq(_count_events("call_resolved"), 1, ...)` before the event is read; (f) the case of m8tv-06.

findings.title: With the window open, turning the radio to music halves the drum's calm; beside the tape the drum adds to it
findings.where: src/core/passenger_sim.gd:421-424 (`_items.radio != ItemSim.MUSIC`); src/core/item_sim.gd:1506-1508 (the radio's rate times the open window's share)
findings.gdd: D-051: 'with the radio on music too it is still one music'. GDD 4.6, Window: 'radio effects are halved'. GDD 8.2: 'music effect without the radio'.
findings.evidence: sim_probes.gd section drum_and_music, Nerves per second over 4 s less the same road alone: 'drum: -0.500', 'drum + radio music: -0.500', 'radio music, window open: -0.250', 'drum + radio music, window open: -0.250', 'mixtape: -1.000', 'drum + mixtape: -1.500'.
findings.failure: He drums and calms at 0.5 a second; the driver, window open, tunes to music and the calm drops to 0.25. With a tape in the deck the drum counts on top of it, so 'one music' holds for the radio only.
findings.fix: While he drums, give the drum's own rate and leave the radio's music out (the larger of the two, not the radio's alone); decide and record whether the tape and the drum add. Append the window row and the tape row to T-PASS-DRUMMER.
